correctness.rationale: The exact update at unmatched odd-degree vertices and matched even-degree vertices is reconstructed. All two-periodic configurations have uniform unmatched groups; individually occupied paired types must return under two successive threshold maps. Integer-only Fourier--Motzkin elimination exhausts 172, 296, and 488 possible regime/support systems in the three matching-defect cases, leaving two, eight, and four real-feasible systems. In the middle case twelve exact additional exclusions force the six two-type populations each to have size q, and direct substitution realizes all solutions for every q>=1. The count equals half the number of nonfixed periodic states. Independent direct vertex update enumerated 1,186,048 states on 22 graphs.

value.rationale: The orbit count for a natural matching-deletion interpolation exhibits an isolated exponential oscillatory resonance: a unique 2-cycle at every k except k=n-1, where 3*binom(n-1,(n-1)/2)+1 cycles exist. This explains a discontinuous edge-restoration effect invisible to generic period restrictions and resolves a complete, motivated infinite-family invariant.
